title: Benchmarking Graph Neural Networks for AC Power Flow: The Role of Inductive Biases and Physical Constraints
abstract: arXiv:2610.38985v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Fast and accurate models for AC power flow (ACPF) are increasingly important as modern electrical grids require more frequent system analyses. Graph neural networks (GNNs) naturally exploit electrical grid topology, yet the effects of architectural design choices on predictive performance remain poorly understood given differences in graph representations and evaluation settings across studies.   We present a unified benchmark of representative GNN architectures for ACPF prediction under a common experimental framework. All models use identical preprocessing and training procedures and comparable parameter budgets, isolating the impact of message-passing mechanisms and inductive biases. We also analyze errors by distance from the slack bus and systematically ablate key design components. translated_abstract: 随着现代电网需要更频繁的系统分析，快速且准确的交流潮流（ACPF）模型正变得日益重要。图神经网络（GNN）天然地利用电网的拓扑结构，但由于各研究在图表示和评估设置上的差异，架构设计选择对预测性能的影响仍然知之甚少。我们在一个统一的实验框架下，对用于ACPF预测的代表性GNN架构进行了统一基准测试。所有模型采用相同的预处理和训练流程以及可比较的参数预算，从而隔离出消息传递机制和归纳偏置的影响。我们还按照与平衡节点的距离对误差进行分析，并系统地消融关键设计组件。我们在IEEE 14节点和IEEE 118节点系统上评估了预测精度和物理一致性。结果表明，各向异性消息传递（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究在统一实验框架下对多种图神经网络架构进行交流潮流预测的基准测试，发现各向异性消息传递机制和物理约束的引入能显著提升预测精度与物理一致性。
en_tdlr: This study benchmarks representative GNN architectures for AC power flow prediction under a unified experimental framework, showing that anisotropic message passing and the incorporation of physical constraints significantly improve predictive accuracy and physical consistency.
